tips.text: Apply for the eVisa only at evisa.gov.vn or thithucdientu.gov.vn: the Immigration Department warns that unofficial sites may charge fees not provided for by Vietnamese regulations.

Enter your full name (surname, middle and given names) exactly as it appears on the ICAO line of your passport, in capital letters. With an e-visa you must enter and leave Viet Nam through the international border gates designated by the Government, though not necessarily the same one.

Canada's travel advice says road safety is poor, fatal accidents often involve motorcycles, and you need a valid Vietnamese driver's licence for any vehicle of 50cc or more, including most motorcycles, that motorcycle riders and passengers must wear a helmet, and that there is zero tolerance for drinking and driving; the UK Foreign Office says British drivers need a 1968 International Driving Permit with their UK licence.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Vietnam?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a visa, and can apply for the official eVisa — 25 USD single entry or 50 USD multiple entry, valid up to 90 days — at evisa.gov.vn (or thithucdientu.gov.vn). Processing normally takes up to 3 working days, or 3 to 15 when the application needs verification.

faq.question: Which nationalities can enter Vietnam without a visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of the countries whose ordinary passports are exempt on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Visa Exemption List (September 2025) enter visa-free. Citizens of the UK, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Japan, South Korea and Russia get 45 days under the unilateral exemption (to 14 March 2028). Citizens of Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia and Switzerland get 45 days for tourism under the Tourism Stimulus Program (to 14 August 2028). Under ASEAN and bilateral agreements, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa exemption list gives ordinary passport holders of Chile and Panama 90 days; Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, Thailand, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia 30 days; the Philippines 21 days; and Brunei 14 days.

faq.question: How much does the Vietnam eVisa cost and how long does it take?
faq.answer: The eVisa costs 25 USD for single entry or 50 USD for multiple entry, is valid for up to 90 days, and is normally processed within 3 working days, or 3 to 15 working days when the application needs verification (working days exclude weekends and public holidays). It is available to citizens of all countries.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Vietnam?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes extending an eVisa. The e-visa portal says an e-visa cannot be applied for from inside Viet Nam, and that e-visa holders in Viet Nam may be eligible for a new visa if invited or guaranteed by an authority, organization or individual in Viet Nam.

faq.question: Does Vietnam require an arrival card or customs declaration?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says that since 15 April 2026 foreign nationals arriving at Tan Son Nhat Airport in Ho Chi Minh City are encouraged to complete a digital arrival card online before arrival; it is not currently mandatory, but this may change or extend to other airports at short notice. You must declare cash over 15 million dong or 5,000 US dollars.
